---
title: "Use of Phreeqcpy package in python"
page-layout: article
---

This is a basic example of using PHREEQC as a module through phreeqpy package. Note the use of the f-string here, which puts a limit on the lowest python version that can be used with such constructions.

The important caveat is that the values in the f-string are substituted linearly. Sometimes it is useful, sometime sit is not. If the variable in the f-string change and the string needs to be updated, a more convenient approach is to use `from string import Template
` and then use the `Template` method `substitute`. All documentation is easily available online.

```python
import phreeqpy.iphreeqc.phreeqc_dll as phreeqc_mod
import pandas as pd


#%% PHREEQC setup

phc1 = phreeqc_mod.IPhreeqc('/home/yutkinm/IPHREEQC/lib/libiphreeqc.so')
db_path = "/home/yutkinm/IPHREEQC/share/doc/iphreeqc/database/phreeqc.dat"
phc1.load_database(db_path)

def get_so(iph):
    out = iph.get_selected_output_array()
    return pd.DataFrame(out[1:], columns=out[0])

#%%
Na = 1
Cl = 1
#%%
pc_input = f"""

SELECTED_OUTPUT 1
reset true

SOLUTION 1
pH 7 charge
Na {Na}
Cl {Cl}
END
"""

phc1.run_string(pc_input)

output = get_so(phc1)

print(output)
```

```text

0    1  i_soln     1   -99.0  ...  0.001       1.0 -2.080965e-17 -1.040374e-12
```
